title: Official Plan Amendment 80 response to province
subtitle: Clair Road housing, NewCold industrial campus, Guelph Innovation District, downtown heights and George Street designation.
overview: Council met in a special meeting to decide what Guelph will tell the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing about the province's reversal of its own changes to Official Plan Amendment 80. Comments were due December 7. Council amended the staff report site by site, then approved the amended report {{vote:m9}}. The mayor said the letter would be made public and would carry the water-capacity concerns raised during debate.

On several sites Council went against staff advice. It asked the province to keep medium density at 41-45 George Street {{vote:m2}}, and to leave the changes for 280 Clair Road West, 384 Crawley Road and the Guelph Innovation District in place {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m6}} {{vote:m7}}. Council also supported removing the provincial employment-zone designation on Clair Road {{vote:m4}}. Downtown, it backed reversing the extra heights while committing to a study of the whole Urban Growth Centre by the end of 2024 {{vote:m5}}.

For residents, these choices affect where affordable housing, large industrial jobs and tall buildings may go. Each site still needs further planning approvals, and the province has not said when it will respond.

decisions.detail: Council asked the province to uphold its July 2022 decision to designate the former industrial site as medium density residential, instead of high density as staff recommended {{vote:m2}}.

Staff are to take no further action on reversing the province's change on this site, and to meet with the housing proponent and encourage a complete application by the end of February 2024 {{vote:m3}}.
Council endorsed removing the provincially significant employment lands designation from the Clair Road site {{vote:m4}}.
Council endorsed reversing the added downtown heights for now, on condition that a study of the entire Urban Growth Centre starts immediately and finishes by Q4 2024 {{vote:m5}}.
Staff are to take no further action on reversing the province's site-specific changes for the proposed industrial campus {{vote:m6}}.
Staff are to take no further action on reversing the province's changes to the district's land use and building height schedules {{vote:m7}}.
Staff are to work with neighbouring businesses and consider their expansion plans in future development applications for the Clair Road site {{vote:m8}}.

Council approved sending the amended report to the province as its comments on OPA 80, directing staff to seek retention of conformity-related changes, prepare cost estimates for the province, and comment on the related planning bill {{vote:m9}}.

debate: Staff said the process was unusual and the timelines short. They urged applicants to come through the front door with a planning application, and warned that rezoning employment land cuts into a limited long-term supply.

The NewCold consultant said reversal could add about a year, risk third-party appeals and lead the company to look elsewhere. Staff said a rezoning would take about four months once complete and that the site plan is already before the Ontario Land Tribunal. Some councillors saw an investment and jobs signal; others said proper process was not a barrier to being open for business.

Clair Road supporters described an affordable ownership model and local employers' need for workforce housing. Councillors and staff raised noise, vibration and setbacks from neighbouring industry, noted that affordability cannot be guaranteed through planning approvals, and said an official plan amendment would still be needed.

On the Guelph Innovation District, staff and some councillors raised the loss of employment land and the strain on water supply. Supporters said the proponent needs long-term certainty, and opponents said the first residential phases could proceed regardless.
A downtown delegate said development is progressing slower than the plan's targets and backed a review of heights across the whole growth centre, though not a blanket 23-storey limit.
